headline: Hatch takes equity stake in Hydrostor and will lead design and execution of the 500 MW Willow Rock project
players: Hydrostor and Hatch announced a strategic execution partnership under which Hatch will lead design and execution for the Willow Rock Energy Storage Center, a 500 MW / 4,000 MWh eight-hour A-CAES facility in California, alongside an equity investment by Hatch in Hydrostor. The investment amount was not disclosed. At announcement Willow Rock was in late-stage development having received final California Energy Commission permitting approvals, with groundbreaking targeted for 2026.
why_it_matters: Hydrostor and Hatch announced a partnership under which Hatch leads design and execution on Willow Rock, a 500 MW / 4,000 MWh eight-hour A-CAES project in California, and takes an equity stake in Hydrostor. That puts Hatch's own capital behind its cost and schedule estimates, partly substituting for the EPC wrap a first-of-a-kind project cannot get. Amount undisclosed, which limits the comfort.
why_you_care: Straight into your Hydrostor work: this is the alignment argument for Willow Rock's bankability and another datapoint on the platform's industrial backing.

headline: MIRATECH completes acquisition of Australia's Exhaust Control Industries, establishing an APAC operating platform
players: MIRATECH completed its acquisition of Exhaust Control Industries, a Melbourne-headquartered manufacturer founded in 1982 that designs and produces exhaust systems, catalytic converters, silencers and turnkey solutions for power generation, industrial, marine and critical infrastructure customers across Australia, New Zealand and Southeast Asia. Financial terms were not disclosed. CEO David Zenthoefer said ECI brings regional expertise, customer relationships and technical capability, and the release cited infrastructure growth, data centers and energy transition pressures as accelerating drivers in Asia Pacific. The transaction was first announced in October 2025.
why_it_matters: Closing turns MIRATECH from an exporter into an in-region APAC manufacturer, which matters in emissions aftertreatment because local fabrication and field service decide who wins work. The data centre driver cited is the same demand thesis running through Sisu. Two deals in six weeks, ECI in February and the ACS catalyst deal in January, signals a programmatic buy-and-build, though undisclosed terms on both mean no multiple read-across.
why_you_care: Your own deal. Progress on the Sisu/MIRATECH platform, and the two-in-six-weeks pace is the buy-and-build story you would tell in a walk-me-through-a-deal answer.

headline: LOGISTEC signs definitive agreement to acquire IPA breakbulk and steel terminal at Port of Altamira, Mexico
players: LOGISTEC entered a definitive agreement to acquire the IPA Terminal at the Port of Altamira, Mexico, a specialised breakbulk and steel handling facility operating under the IPA, ATEMSA, SMA and STEEL entities with deepwater access. Price was not disclosed. Completion remains subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals from Mexico's Comisión Nacional Antimonopolio and the Mexican Port Authorities and Navy, with no timeline provided. Berenson & Company advised on financial matters and Holland & Knight on legal. CEO Sean Pierce framed the deal as accelerated international growth extending LOGISTEC's network to Latin America.
why_it_matters: LOGISTEC's first Latin American move: a steel and breakbulk terminal at Altamira that pairs with Houston into a two-country steel corridor rather than two standalone terminals. Signed but not closed, with Mexican antitrust plus port authority and Navy clearance outstanding and no timetable, so the approval path is less predictable than a US filing. With Dubuque and the Houston cranes, Blue Wolf is building a Gulf-plus-inland network.
why_you_care: You worked LOGISTEC/Termont, so this is your own situation moving. Closing confirmation and the Mexican approval path are what to track next.

headline: Hydrostor signs 50 MW Willow Rock offtake with California Community Power on behalf of six CCAs
players: Hydrostor signed a 50 MW offtake agreement for the Willow Rock Energy Storage Center with California Community Power acting for six member community choice aggregators: CleanPowerSF, Peninsula Clean Energy, Redwood Coast Energy Authority, San Jose Clean Energy, Silicon Valley Clean Energy Authority and Valley Clean Energy Authority. Term length was not disclosed. The project received its California Energy Commission permit in December 2025 and a franchise agreement from the Kern County Board of Supervisors, and is expected online in 2030.
why_it_matters: Contracted capacity is what lets lenders size debt, so this is the milestone that makes the DOE conditional commitment financeable. But 50 MW against 500 MW of nameplate means only a tenth of the project is sold; the rest needs more offtake or merchant CAISO exposure. The six-CCA counterparty group is fragmented, which lenders will scrutinise.
why_you_care: You worked Hydrostor, so this is the number that anchors Willow Rock's contracted share, and the gap you would have to defend in any valuation.
